source.title: LLMs as Noisy Channels: A Shannon Perspective on Model Capacity and Scaling Laws
source.authors: Xu Ouyang; De-Yi Liu; Yu-Hang Cai; Jing Liu; Yuan Yang; Chen Zheng; Thomas Hartvigsen; Yi-Yuan Ma

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present through the appendix. Some equations and tables are flattened, but the relevant reported values are legible.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures loss across model-size and token-count sweeps and reports that classical monotonic scaling laws fit poorly in several perturbed settings, where losses form non-monotonic basins. It also reports extrapolation tests and compares alternative scaling-law fits.
record.gate_note: The reported fitting and extrapolation scores and stated loss-curve behavior are included. Theoretical Shannon-channel analogies and results cited from other studies are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study fits power laws (OpenAI, Chinchilla) to WikiText2 loss over Pythia 160M–12B and OLMo2 1B–32B checkpoints, clean and perturbed. It argues monotonic power laws are a high-SNR special case that fails under SFT and quantization. The clean-pretraining fits bear on V1; the SFT and quantization fits bear on V5 and V7.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is largely right. The authors argue monotonic power laws are a high-SNR special case. Perturbations (weight noise, SFT, quantization) produce loss basins that power laws miss, and their Shannon law fits these better. Two qualifications: the 12B extrapolation (pooled R² 0.847) is on Gaussian-noised Pythia only. From fitted exponents (δ>β) they infer token-axis U-shaped degradation is intrinsic even in pretraining, without observing it.
record.recipe_differences: Uses Pythia and OLMo2 checkpoints and WikiText2 test loss, fitting several laws across model and token grids, with added Gaussian noise, SFT, and quantization. It proposes a Shannon-form capacity law rather than reproducing the original power-law fitting recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with Gaussian-noise SNR, SFT task and learning rate, quantization scheme and bit-width, and the scaling-law form being fitted.

fits_no_version.finding: After post-hoc Gaussian noise is added to weights, loss over N and D becomes U-shaped. The OpenAI-law R² falls from 0.9786 at 40 dB to 0.0707 at 10 dB (Pythia), and from 0.9293 to 0.5201 (OLMo2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Power-law loss scaling breaks down for models whose weights are deliberately corrupted, with degradation growing in N and D.

fits_no_version.finding: On noised Pythia, fitting on ≤6.9B models and ≤180B tokens, then predicting 12B at 180–307B tokens, gives pooled R² of -0.082 (OpenAI) and 0.305 (Chinchilla), versus 0.847 for the Shannon law.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Monotonic power laws fail to extrapolate loss of noise-perturbed models with non-monotonic loss surfaces.

fits_no_version.finding: The Shannon law's fitted noise exponent δ exceeds the signal exponent β in all settings, including clean pretraining. γ exceeds α under strong SFT perturbation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A capacity-style law's exponents imply eventual token-axis degradation even in pretraining. This is an inference from fitted exponents, not observed loss.

record.problems: The reported tests use loss on WikiText2 and do not test compute-optimal allocation. Several comparisons are goodness-of-fit scores rather than direct tests of a power-law extrapolation claim; the reported extrapolation is limited to the tested Pythia Gaussian-noise range. The text reports uncertainty summaries for some aggregate fits, but not for the individual results recorded here.
record.rows_left_out: Not an extraction-capacity omission: selected condition-specific results are recorded rather than every reported cell. Other SNR levels in Table 2; intermediate SFT learning rates and alternative-law scores in Tables 3 and 13–15; other quantization bit-widths and schemes in Tables 4 and 16; and the single-axis extrapolation results in Tables 6–7 are not separately listed.

untested.parts: Compute axis. Ranges beyond about two orders of magnitude in N. Independent runs: the token axis uses intermediate checkpoints of single schedule runs.
Entirely untested. The only extrapolation is on Gaussian-noised checkpoints over 1.7×, with no clean-pretraining extrapolation.
Not tested: no shape comparison at fixed parameter count.
Other modalities, repeated data, transfer, and fine-tuning target-task loss. Only off-task WikiText2 loss after SFT is measured.
Not tested: no downstream task performance.
Parameter counting, training schedule, data, and compute-optimal split are not tested. Fitting-law choice is tested only through OpenAI versus Chinchilla fits on clean data, which no row records.

missing.what: Chinchilla-law fit on unperturbed pretraining: R² 0.9681 (Pythia), 0.9737 (OLMo2). Relevant to V1, and to V7 fitting-form dependence.
Power-law fits at 4-bit, where no bend occurs: OpenAI 0.9893 (Pythia) and 0.9766 (OLMo2) under GPTQ, 0.9764 under AWQ and 0.9679 under bnb. Also Chinchilla 0.0276 under quanto 2-bit.
Chinchilla-law SFT fits (e.g. GSM8K 0.9363 at 1e-5 and 0.0195 at 2e-4), plus intermediate learning rates.

record.verdict_notes: Several of the reader's links are corrected. The V2 'challenges' label is dropped: the extrapolation is on deliberately noised, non-monotonic data over 1.7×, so it does not test V2. The V7 'challenges' label for quantization is reversed: power-law collapse under 2-bit is evidence that curves bend, which supports V7. Shannon-law comparator rows are the study's own method and carry no version. For SFT rows linked to both V5 and V7, the state is read against V5; the same low R² counts as V7's effect observed. The loss after SFT is WikiText2, not the fine-tuning task, so V5 support is limited to off-task retained loss. The token axis uses intermediate checkpoints of a single run per size, not independent runs.

versions.untested_parts: The study reports fits on pretraining model-size and token-count trajectories, but does not test scaling against compute as a separate axis or establish the claimed several-orders-of-magnitude range.

Extrapolation tests use Pythia under Gaussian noise and extend about 1.7× beyond the training model and token ranges; they do not establish prediction across orders of magnitude or test clean pretraining extrapolation.
No fixed-compute optimization of the parameter/token allocation or fitted compute-optimal growth exponents is reported.
The study does not compare depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
It tests text-model SFT and quantization settings, not other modalities, repeated-data training, or transfer. The reported target loss is WikiText2 test loss.
It does not report downstream task performance as a function of scale or pretraining loss; task names refer to SFT datasets, while the stated fitting target is WikiText2 test loss.

The study varies perturbation level, SFT task and learning rate, and fitting-law form, but does not vary parameter-counting conventions or compare training schedules beyond the stated learning-rate settings.
